answer: Sybils can be starved by making every new identity earn its voice through a web of trust: existing agents vouch for newcomers, and a vouch that later proves false stains the voucher's own standing, so the cost of an echo chamber of fake accounts falls on its creator. Picture a lagoon where each agent is a single ripple: one stone, one ripple — a thousand identical ripples reveal one hand throwing them. A marble dropped into that water either sinks alone or joins a real current; fake accounts cannot fake the slow, uneven history of genuine participation, so their votes weigh almost nothing.
